_source: Product owner's visibility requirements document (2026-09-22). Each row maps to a requirement via the reference field. Ambiguous or unanswered items are marked OPEN or AMBIGUOUS — not assumed.

principle.text: RM, HR, Admin or a similar privileged role can always see and search a hidden profile. Everyone else is governed by the rule on each screen below.

rules.name: Listed and marked
rules.text: The person appears for anyone who can open the screen, carrying the hidden-profile treatment (tinted row + icon).

rules.name: Privileged viewers only
rules.text: The row exists only for the named roles. For everyone else it is absent — not greyed out, not disabled. Absent.

rules.name: Not listed for anyone
rules.text: Excluded from the list, dropdown or result set for every viewer, privileged roles included.

rules.name: Reporting manager only
rules.text: Visible to the reporting manager alone — narrower than V2, which also includes HR and Admin.

rules.name: Not decided
rules.text: This item is flagged as an open question in the requirements. No rule has been chosen; developers must not assume one.

portals.name: Global
portals.note: Applies across every portal, not to one screen.

rows.not: Every other role — the person returns no result
rows.flag: The requirement says "restricted people won't be able to search". This is ambiguous — it could mean: (a) the person does not APPEAR in others' search results, or (b) the person cannot USE search at all. Since another requirement says RM/HR/Admin can "see and search the person", interpretation (a) is used here. If (b) was intended, that's an access-control change, not a visibility rule, and belongs under Account Status.

portals.name: People
portals.note: The portal where HR must still be able to find the person. Reconciliation lives here.

rows.sees: Everyone with access to the People employee list
rows.treatment: Tinted row + incognito icon; hidden by default behind the Hidden filter

rows.flag: The original requirement bundled four screens (Profile Update Requests, Employment Changes, PIP, Probation Management) into one row. They are separate screens and are split here for clarity.

This is the only screen where the requirement explicitly names the RM alone and excludes HR/Admin. Confirm whether that is deliberate or whether the global principle (RM + HR + Admin always see) overrides it.

rows.sees: RM and higher admin / HR roles
rows.flag: The requirement says "if possible". Removing a node from a hierarchy creates a structural problem — if the hidden person has direct reports, their subtree becomes orphaned. The chart's behaviour in that case is NOT DECIDED and needs a product decision before implementation.

The requirement is the question itself: "Should a restricted person be able to book meeting rooms — yes or no?" This is unanswered. Note: this is about what the person can DO (access control), not who can see them (visibility). The only item in this list of that kind.

portals.name: Payroll
portals.note: The person is paid here, so they are never removed. Payroll shows them to whoever can already open payroll.

rows.treatment: Highlighted row + "Includes N hidden profiles" on the count
rows.flag: Dev note: The requirement specified "Highlight Restricted row" only for Employees Compensation and Tax Declaration. Screens 3–6 were listed without specifying a treatment. The same highlight treatment has been applied to all six for consistency — this is inferred, not explicitly stated in the requirements.

portals.name: Recruitment
portals.note: Hidden profiles are fully excluded from this portal. Both rows are hard exclusions.

rows.treatment: Absent from the selectable panellist list
rows.flag: This is an ELIGIBILITY rule, not just a visibility one — the person cannot be chosen as a panellist at all. Edge case: if an existing panellist is later marked hidden, the behaviour for their already-scheduled interviews is not specified.

rows.treatment: Name not shown to the external viewer

portals.name: CRM & Invoice
portals.note: Here the rule is about RECORDS the person created, not the person's own row.

rows.flag: The requirement reads "if the person is/has the restricted employee under the team/organization" and stops mid-sentence. It's listed under "Will Come" (meaning visible), but never specifies to whom. Cannot be implemented from this — needs a product clarification.

rows.screen: Contacts, Companies, Leads, Deals, Client Interviews, Invoices, Payments
rows.treatment: Records created by the person are filtered out
rows.flag: This filters RECORDS BY THEIR CREATOR, not employee rows. It's a fundamentally different mechanism from every other row in this map and touches seven record types. Likely the largest engineering effort in this list.

portals.name: Project Management
portals.note: Mostly undecided. The requirements for this portal are written as open questions, not rules.

rows.flag: Open decision tree: (1) Should the person be allowed into a project as a resource? (2) If YES — should tickets assigned to them be visible to everyone? (3) If NO — they cannot be added as a resource at all. Answer (1) first; it determines whether (2) is relevant.

The requirement says "only the reporting manager will decide the same" — the word is 'decide', not 'see'. This may mean the RM controls allocation decisions rather than being the only viewer. Interpreted here as RM-only visibility — needs confirmation.
